text: Baseline refuted (E0002, local-full, full precision, n=200, seed 1): the loaded checkpoint reproduces the dataset answers on only 12% of prompts, at or below chance (1/6 = 16.7% uniform; the labels are skewed to 'bo', so a constant guesser would do better). Logit differences are of order 1e7 with mean -2.9e6 and std 2.1e7, i.e. sign-random and numerically blown up, not a calibrated readout. The dataset labels themselves (E0001, n=64, seed 0) are all consistent with 'minimum of the 5 input tokens under the order bo < nu < pa < la < {ri, vu}' (ri vs vu not resolved in the sample), but that is a property of the labels, not of this model: the model does not compute it.

Stop after the baseline. The model does not perform the behaviour (accuracy 0.12, E0002), so there is no mechanism to localise; any heads/MLPs surfaced by patching against a chance-level metric with 1e7-scale logits would be noise. No circuit is claimed and no verify_hypothesis is run, since a circuit claim would be unsupported. 23 of 25 experiments left unspent.
